rationale: A wins because it knows where the facts stop. Its data-residency angle says, "There is no supplied regulatory event to peg this to, and none should be implied"; that is adult supervision. B has useful raw material, but then it pitches "Notion's compliance stack puts Confluence and SharePoint on the defensive," which is a competitive story the update did not earn.
gaps_in_A: "after it added customer-held encryption keys" leans into causality the update only implies through Notion's own framing; keep the attribution tighter.
"bank and hospital compliance" is half-supported. The update mentions healthcare as a blocked category, but gives only bank pilots.
"How Notion made a shared editor work with no connection at all" is a good engineering angle, but it needs limits fast; otherwise it can drift into generic product deep-dive territory.
gaps_in_B: "anchored in named institutions" is wrong. The update says four of the five largest US banks, not which banks.
"Notion's compliance stack puts Confluence and SharePoint on the defensive" invents competitors, displacement pressure, and market consequences not in the facts.
"in a year when most software compounds connectivity" is a fake contrarian peg. Sounds clever, proves nothing.
"forced to localize data for Europe and Australia" overstates the data-residency fact and implies regulatory pressure the update never supplied.
